## 2026-09-07 integrated acceptance refinement
Execution plan lives in #803; no duplicate implementation scope here.

Use one compatible revision, executable/build, map/Experience, settings and selected content set. Preserve the existing base/Core/shop selections until a better qualified replacement is proven. Stock Fox is excluded; Tiny3D owns generated rigging.

Required normal-user sequence:
1. Start solo versus AI; separately host/join LAN with two real player perspectives. Say exactly which routes were tested; local two-instance proof does not establish Internet play.
2. Find the lane, opponent/Core, shop, controls and first useful action from normal UI without developer commands.
3. Fight with visible character/spell state; ski/grapple a useful route in both first-/third-person.
4. Edit terrain, place a defense and destroy/reopen it; observe the same collision/navigation result on both sides.
5. Earn and spend gold; see the changed lane pressure/upgrade effect.
6. Defeat/respawn and character swap preserve the declared state; Core defeat gives correct replicated result.
7. Rematch/restart/return through the existing UI; no leaked input, actors, timers, abilities, gold or old result state.

Attach a short chaptered normal-play sequence plus exact proof/trace references. Diagnostic close-ups supplement it for contact/deformation; they do not substitute for play. Independent review must inspect pixels, not only receipt fields. Retain raw evidence and exact content/package dependencies so replay survives relocation/link expiry.

Report incomplete steps honestly. #2610 owns missing full animation coverage; #2611 owns the measured combined workload. No new proof harness is requested.

---

Parent convergence issue: #803  ## What the user actually wants  A single playable V2 match that feels like a game, not a collection of disconnected systems.  ### Core match - **2 opposing bases**. - **1 clear road/lane** connecting them. - **Creeps spawn continuously** and travel down that road toward the enemy base/core. - Killing/playing around creeps and elapsed match play produces **gold**. - Gold can be spent on meaningful match actions/upgrades. - Playable as **1v1 versus AI** or **multiplayer 1v1**.  ### Terrain and routing - **Earthworks** must work during the match. - Players can raise/lower terrain, dig trenches, make ramps/berms/high ground, and otherwise reshape the battlefield. - Terrain edits must affect **real traversal**. - Terrain edits must also affect **creep routing**: creeps should reroute around blocked paths or follow newly viable paths instead of ignoring terrain changes.  ### Building and destruction - Players can **build defenses/walls/assets** around the base and lane. - These structures are **destructible**. - Destruction must visibly reopen or change routes. - Building + destruction + earthworks must all coexist in the same match and influence players/creeps rather than being separate demos.  ### Player movement and characters - **Tribes-style skiing/momentum** is usable in the real match. - **Grappling hook** works in the real match. - **Character swapping** works from a usable roster rather than a placeholder pawn. - Character swaps preserve a usable gameplay experience with correct scale/orientation/animation.  ### Combat and spells - The player has **skills/spells** in the match. - Spells must be visibly readable and functional, including the **meteor** path. - Spells interact with the actual battlefield/enemies rather than only appearing in a proof/demo path.  ## Required integrated experience  The intended result is:  > Spawn into a 1v1 match, choose/swap a character, move with normal controls + skiing + grapple, fight using spells, earn gold from lane play, build and destroy defenses, reshape the terrain with earthworks, and watch creeps reroute through the changed battlefield while two bases fight across one clear road/lane.  This should work in either **player vs AI** or **player vs player** form.  ## Acceptance  Do not call this complete because individual source systems, unit tests, or isolated PIE probes pass. The normal user launch must visibly prove on one compatible head:  1. Two visible opposing bases and one readable connecting road/lane. 2. Creeps spawn, move down the lane, fight, and target the opposing base/core. 3. Gold increases from creep/match play and is spendable. 4. 1v1 works against AI and multiplayer 1v1 remains supported. 5. Earthworks visibly changes terrain during the match. 6. Creeps reroute when terrain/building changes block or alter their route. 7. Building works and placed walls/assets are destructible. 8. Destruction visibly changes traversal/routing again. 9. Skiing is real momentum/slope movement, not a short dash. 10. Grappling hook is visibly usable in the real match. 11. Character swapping works with correctly scaled/oriented/animated characters. 12. Spells/skills work, including meteor, with visible cast/impact/result. 13. All of the above is tested through the same ordinary human-facing launch path, not disconnected developer-only demos.  ## Non-goal  Do not rebuild duplicate systems that already exist. Converge the existing V2/Tiny3D/gameplay work into this one playable result and fix missing runtime bindings/assets/presentation where they prevent the experience above. 
### Base composition must use the user's real assets
- Each side must have a visibly composed **base area**, not a floating/default pawn in an empty map.
- The **Core must use the user's intended Core asset(s)** already selected for V2; primitive placeholders or generic dummy meshes do not count.
- Each base must visibly include the previously required **house/base structure, surrounding wall/defence pieces, shop, Core, and readable base dressing**.
- The shop must be a real visible/interactable part of the base/economy loop, not only a hidden actor or code path.
- The road/lane must physically and visually connect the two completed bases.
- Existing user assets already admitted through P3/Tiny3D should be used where they are the intended product assets. Do not replace them with temporary cubes, mannequins, untextured stand-ins, or invisible actors for acceptance.
- Scale, orientation, materials/textures and placement must be visibly correct in the normal launch. A giant sideways character, floating pawn, missing material, or off-map asset is a failure.

comments.body: Independent validation of clean unpublished branch `chatgpt/issue941-convergence-20260904` at `98e2957e`: focused #941 contracts passed for human launch, camera/character controls, production character, road routing, base composition, core binding/presentation, skiing, jump, grapple/dash traversal, economy/gold HUD, creep routing/readability, flying enemies, match result/melee/defeat presentation, construction/destruction/paint, plus the Earthworks performance-wrapper regression (2/2); `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` also passed. The branch carries four product commits plus local `e9c7504f` queue-wait guard work; GitHub `main` advanced from `52c58bc2` to `cc7d1933` via #961, which supersedes that build-only lane, so convergence should preserve the four product commits and drop/reconcile `e9c7504f`. Publication failed before ref upload because this machine's Git/LFS credential route resolves through unavailable `127.0.0.1:1`; exactly two LFS objects are pending (Fennec and Sealdiver Experience assets). I did not retry or change credential/network configuration. No PR exists yet; heavy integrated runtime proof remains pending while another RenderOffscreen Unreal process owns the lane.

Cross-agent cache unblock for the current human-launch path: I audited head `5bb3df57e` without mutating this claimed worktree. `Get-P3HumanLaunchTrackedContent` resolves 436 player-facing files. All 436 are currently pointers in this lane; 376 already had local LFS objects and 60 were missing (268.1 MiB). Every one of those 60 OIDs had an exact hydrated counterpart in the primary P3 checkout. I seeded those 60 objects into the shared LFS cache with size + SHA-256 verification only; no remote fetch and no checkout/mutation in this worktree.

Receipt: `P3_941_CACHE_SEED=PASS seeded=60 seeded_bytes=281130428 required_missing_cache=0`.

So the existing local-only hydration in `launch_lane_war_human_1v1.ps1` should now be able to materialize its full bounded required set from cache instead of failing on those 60 objects.

PR #969 is now published at exact head `5bb3df57e`. Canonical two-object LFS publication PASS with persistent guards unchanged; changed Python contract suites PASS; native `P3Gameplay` hot-source build PASS (`Result: Succeeded`, 737.27s). The issue remains open for ordinary human-facing integrated runtime acceptance.

Convergence update: #969 merged as `588b81beba0c019cbf693c967ab0d6f0dc7746ee` after hosted contract gate PASS on exact head `fbb610b5e`. During convergence, the first gate failure was reproduced and fixed by removing controller-side explicit `UnPossess()` from character cycling; the full CI-selected changed-area set then passed 25/25. Two stale Lane War source contracts were also updated to the current robust creep reward attribution and authored Weathered Rune Bridge road behavior; integrated product contract sets passed 30/30 and 29/29 locally. Duplicate implementation PR #967 was closed as superseded. #941 remains open for ordinary human-facing integrated runtime/visual acceptance.

Maple convergence: two prerequisites that previously obscured ordinary playable acceptance are now landed/closed. #963 runtime pointer admission is fixed by #969, and #973 persistent replicated hero health is fixed by #974. Current main therefore has the bounded hydrated human launch, solo AI/melee/reward convergence, and authoritative hero HP state. Keep #941 open for the actual ordinary integrated human-facing runtime/visual acceptance; do not reopen those prerequisite implementation slices.

Tracked as #982; it deliberately avoids the active health-file mutation scope until that lane lands.

Combat convergence advanced: #980 landed replicated hero HP/defeated state in the first/third-person combat HUD (`a979f38b`), and #981 landed normal Unreal point-damage routing into authoritative combat health after hosted gate success. Next combat seam is #982 authoritative defeat -> respawn.

Coordination checkpoint (not ownership authority): the canonical coordinator now has `p3:worktree:user-v2-test` held by `ChatGPT:p3-swarm-coordinator-20260905` for the final human acceptance lane. I will not mutate the exact files currently owned by other actors.

Heavy-work policy for this lane: builds go through the existing global single-flight build slot; no duplicate P3 render/runtime is launched on top of another heavy P3 runtime; render-offscreen proofs use the merged #996 receipt-pinned pressure guard. The 04:53 Showroom termination was verified intentional pressure relief against the positively owned proof, not an unexplained crash. The `current-main-runtime-owner` snapshot now contains the #996 pressure-guard code. Final Lane War acceptance continues only after a live process/pressure check and without disturbing foreign exact claims.

Taking a disjoint player-visible #941 slice: replace the Lane War shop's Engine BasicShape cylinder placeholder with an existing Building15 visual-PASS production asset through config-owned presentation. Scope is only the shop actor presentation binding, normal human-launch hydration for that exact asset, and focused economy regression coverage. No TowerDefenseFeatureActor/GameMode/input mutation and no heavy Unreal run while other lanes own it.

incoming change resolution: p3:scripts/launch_lane_war_human_1v1.ps1 is currently claimed by ChatGPT-Sol-803-creep-hydration-20260905. I initially intended to add one shop-asset hydration path there; no mutation occurred. I am avoiding that collision entirely by binding the shop to the already-hydrated Building15 visual-PASS WeatheredWoodWallBrace family instead, so the incoming launch-script change is superseded and requires no action from the claimant.

2026-09-05 acceptance audit: the existing `P3_RUNTIME_LANEWAR_ACCEPTANCE RESULT=PASS` / `LANEWAR_LISTEN_FULL_MATCH_ACCEPTANCE=PASS` is **not sufficient to close #941**. Its current final marker proves only: two players/listen host+client, teams, cores, dash, grapple, both-side respawn, player-to-core faction damage, creep spawn/attack, core defeat/winner/match-over, and creep spawn stop.

It does **not** prove the user-facing requirements that caused the failed self-test: authored base/house/walls/shop/road presentation, qualified animated creeps, Tribes skiing, Earthworks terrain edit + creep reroute, construction + destructible walls/assets, spells/meteor, visible environment/grass/time-of-day, or character presentation/swap quality. Keep this runtime as a combat/network gate only. #941 remains open until those are visibly exercised through the ordinary product launch.

Taking only the existing human-launch hydration manifest + its existing source contract, plus verified local-cache seeding of those 9 OIDs; no remote fetch, gameplay code, world-builder, or heavy runtime mutation.

Combat-composition resume audit: the stale WIP that creates `/Game/V2/AS_V2Combat` should not be published. No commit, push, or PR was made from `chatgpt/941-combat-composition-20260905`. #941 remains the broader integrated human-facing acceptance task.

Continuation on an unowned source-only environment acceptance seam. Current production-world authoring still spawns fixed P3_V2_KeyLight + P3_V2_SkyFill actors even though AP3EnvironmentPresentationDirector is the canonical time/weather presentation owner (sun, moon, sky atmosphere, skylight, fog). Those fixed lights were added later in #414 and can keep the battlefield lit independently of replicated time-of-day. Proof: focused world/environment source contracts 18/18 PASS, py_compile PASS, diff-check PASS, hosted contract gate SUCCESS. Unowned acceptance seam: current Grapple has direct GAS/two-client runtime proof (#910) but the canonical scripts/v2/verification/p3_pie_adapter.py ordinary-input path does not support Input.Traversal.Grapple.
